explain.say: The oceans have a giant, slow loop of currents called the global conveyor belt, or thermohaline circulation. Thermo means heat and haline means salt, the two things that drive it.

faq.q: How do ocean currents carry heat?
faq.a: Water stores lots of heat. Warm currents like the Gulf Stream carry heat from the tropics towards the poles, and cold currents bring cold water back, evening out Earth's temperatures.

faq.q: Why does cold salty water sink?
faq.a: Cold water is denser than warm water, and salty water is denser than fresh water. So cold, salty water is the heaviest and sinks beneath the lighter water around it.

A strong, warm current that flows from the Gulf of Mexico up the east coast of the United States and across the Atlantic towards Europe. It carries far more water than all the world's rivers combined.
asks: Where does the Gulf Stream go?

faq.q: How long does the conveyor belt take?
faq.a: Deep water moves only a few centimetres per second, so a full loop around the world's oceans is estimated to take about 1,000 years.
asks: How fast are deep ocean currents?

faq.q: Could the conveyor belt slow down?
faq.a: Scientists think it could. Melting ice adds fresh water to the North Atlantic, making the surface water less salty and less likely to sink, and there are signs the Atlantic part has weakened.
asks: Is climate change affecting ocean currents?

facts: Thermohaline comes from Greek words meaning heat and salt.
The Gulf Stream carries about 30 million cubic metres of water per second off Florida, and much more further north.

quiz.say: Why does water sink near Greenland to start the deep current?

options.show: It becomes cold and salty, so it is dense
options.say: It becomes cold and salty, so it is dense

quiz.why: Cooling and the salt left behind by forming sea ice make the water dense, so it sinks to the deep ocean.

wrong.1: Whales are far too small to move whole ocean currents.
wrong.2: Snow adds a little fresh water, which actually makes surface water lighter, not heavier.
